answer: The Gemara explains why Rabbi Akiva was called the head of all the sages: As it is taught in a baraita: There was an incident involving Rabbi Akiva, who was confined in a prison, and Rabbi Yehoshua HaGarsi would attend to him and serve him every day. Every day, they would bring him water in a measure sufficient for his needs. One day, the superintendent of the prison found Rabbi Yehoshua and said to him: Today your water is excessive; perhaps you need it to soften the walls of the prison and thereby undermine them? He poured out half the water and gave him the other half. When Rabbi Yehoshua came to Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Akiva said to him: Yehoshua, do you not know that I am old and my life depends on your life? No one else attends to me, and if you cause me to lose my life, you will have no one to attend to me. Rabbi Yehoshua told him the entire incident. Rabbi Akiva said to him: Give me water to wash my hands. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: There is not enough water even for you to drink. Rabbi Akiva said to him: What can I do? They issued a decree that one who does not wash his hands before eating is liable to receive death at the hands of Heaven. It is preferable that I die my own death by thirst and not transgress the opinion of my colleagues. They said that he would not taste anything until Rabbi Yehoshua brought him water and he washed his hands. When the Sages heard about this, they said: If he was so exacting in his piety in his old age, how much more so must he have been in his youth. And if he was so exacting in prison, how much more so must he have been when not in prison.
